title: Work IQ: business skills for agents through Work IQ MCP

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing says administrators must opt in, but Microsoft documents automatic enablement for eligible environments, including existing environments starting in November 2026. It also overstates role requirements, omits activation when describing skill updates, and incorrectly reports that MCP client automation and cloud information are undocumented.

claims.claim: The roadmap was modified at 2026-11-11T00:53:34.
Business skills are natural-language instructions capturing organisational processes.
claims.quote: Business skills are natural-language instructions that capture how your organization gets work done. They represent your business processes, policies, and domain knowledge in a format that agents can understand and follow.

claims.claim: A skill describes steps, required information and business rules for completing work.
claims.quote: Each skill describes how to complete a specific type of work—the steps involved, the information required, and the business rules that apply.

claims.claim: Agents discover and use accessible skills at runtime through Work IQ MCP.
claims.quote: Agents discover and use the business skills they have access to as needed at runtime using Work IQ MCP to complete tasks according to your organization's processes.

claims.claim: Multiple agents can use the same skill to follow the same process.
claims.quote: When multiple agents use the same skill, they follow the same process, ensuring consistent behavior across your organization.

claims.claim: Business skills are stored in Dataverse.
claims.quote: Business skills are stored in Dataverse and follow Dataverse security patterns.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes business skills as a preview feature.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: Skill frontmatter contains a name, description and metadata.
claims.quote: Frontmatter | Name, description, and optional key-value metadata

claims.claim: Skills contain instructions and attached resource files.
claims.quote:
Instructions | Full skill body | Contains the complete process definition
Resources | Attached reference files

claims.claim: Agents query frontmatter and retrieve full instructions only when needed.
claims.quote: Agents query frontmatter to find applicable skills, then retrieve full instructions and resources only when needed.

claims.claim: Business skills are not executable code.
claims.quote: Business skills are not executable code. They contain natural-language instructions that guide agent behavior

claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator can enable business skills by turning on Work IQ in a Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: To enable business skills in a Dataverse environment, a Power Platform administrator turns on Work IQ.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: Business skills are admin-opt-in and require an administrator to turn on Work IQ before use in every environment.
claims.quote: Starting in November 2026, Microsoft turns on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to on. Explain that Work IQ is enabled by default for eligible public production environments: new environments from September 30, 2026 and existing environments starting November 2026. Carry the EU/EFTA preview, government-related and nonproduction exceptions. Replace the universal admin-opt-in wording in Why it matters and Scope with a requirement that Work IQ be enabled, automatically or manually. Report this alongside the overview's manual-enablement guidance.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Skill selection is probabilistic, and Microsoft recommends descriptive names and representative tests before broad sharing.
claims.quote: Write a description that states both what the skill does and when to use it. Agent selection is probabilistic, so test representative requests before you share a skill broadly.

claims.claim: Resources can contain policy or process material whose access is controlled through skill sharing.
claims.quote: Provides supporting documents, templates, policies, and other materials agents can use when following the skill

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Skill creation, modification and use follow ownership, sharing and Dataverse security roles.
claims.quote: Governance—Control who can create, modify, and use business skills through ownership, sharing, and Dataverse security roles.

claims.claim: Users need the Skill Sharing Role as well as the selected role.
claims.quote: Users who access a skill through a Dataverse security role must have both the selected role and the Skill Sharing Role security role.
claims.fix: Qualify the sentence: 'Users accessing a skill through security-role sharing need both the selected Dataverse security role and Skill Sharing Role. General access and direct sharing are separate access methods.'

claims.claim: Skills guide agents using connected tools to carry out the process.
claims.quote:
The agent retrieves the complete instructions and resources for a relevant skill.

claims.claim: Editing one skill changes behaviour across all agents that use it.
claims.quote: Save | Saves your working copy without changing the version agents use. A new skill remains inactive. If the skill already has an active version, that version stays active.
claims.fix: Replace with 'Activating an updated skill changes the instructions available to agents that use it; editing and saving a working copy alone does not change the active version.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-business-skills#save-and-activate-a-business-skill.

claims.claim: Allowed MCP Clients is accessible through the environment Features page, Dataverse Model Context Protocol and Advanced Settings in Power Platform admin center.

In the Dataverse Model Context Protocol section, select Go to Advanced Settings.
In the Active Allowed MCP Clients list, find Enterprise Copilot Platform and verify that Is Enabled is set to Yes.

claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for Allowed MCP Clients, and none of the listed settings has a documented API.
claims.quote:
An MCP client that is allowed to talk to MCP endpoint
Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients
Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE
isenabled | Edm.Boolean | Display name: Is Enabled
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api null with the documented allowedmcpclient Web API surface: the allowedmcpclients entity set supports PATCH and exposes the writable isenabled Boolean. Cite this reference, update the rendered table and remove the blanket claim that none has an API. For adding allowed clients, the documented command is dataverse mcp allow <appId>, at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/cli/reference.

Review its current availability.
